transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Ana (Copperline SRE), Tom (Copperline ML), Priya (Copperline PM)
Recording note: partial audio drop around 00:22:30 - minor gaps

Summary:
Redwood ran a console-focused debugging playbook demo for Copperline to show request tracing, error forensics, and how to triage degraded responses back to model variants or infra fallbacks. Customer is focused on production incidents where in-flight requests return partial generations or time out; main constraints: PCI-like data residency, strict SSO, and budget for Dedicated capacity.

Topics covered:
- Console request timeline and trace stitching
- KV cache hits/misses and implications for latency and token cost
- Fallback policies: model variant routing, regional failover
- Request replay and hypothesis testing in a sandbox
- Integration points for audit logs and SSO/SAML

Links shared:
- deck: https://redwood.example/decks/provenance-playbook (shared during call)
- sample harness: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/trace-harness
- security summary doc: link noted, to be shared after call

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll do a quick 5 minute intro and then jump into the console, show a live failure case and then run a replay - sound good?
[00:18] Ana: yep that's perfect, thanks. we have Tom and I, and Priya might drop in a bit late.
[00:25] Tom: yep i'm here, thanks. main thing for us - we've been seeing these partial generations that sort of time out at 400-500ms but our app shows them as incomplete responses, and it's hard to map them back to service-side traces, so hoping to see the request-to-token path.
[00:40] Leo: great, we built a debug playbook for exactly that - it's about stitching request logs with per-token traces and the KV cache signals so you can see whether it's a model slow-down, an infra GC or a cache miss. you'll see a live case in a sec.
[00:55] Priya (on join): apologies for the delay, joining now.
[01:05] Maya: no worries, ok so quick context - Copperline is evaluating hosted vs dedicated and also private network options, right? what are the gating questions?
[01:17] Ana: security first - SSO and retention policies, also residency for some PII-ish fields. then performance - sub-200ms tail is our target for 95th for small prompts. cost is the long pole but performance and reliability are deal breakers.
[01:33] Maya: totally, we'll show the console features that map to each. Leo will start screen share with a reproduced error trace.
[01:45] Leo: ok sharing. first screen is the request explorer - you can filter by route, model, and time. here's a request id: req_9b3f2a that Ana sent beforehand. you can see status code 504, partial tokens flagged in the transcript buffer.
[02:12] [screen noise] Speaker 2: uh hm
[02:18] Leo: the trace view stitches the API gateway span, the runtime span, and the model span. note the k-v cache hit header - in our logs it's 'x-kv-hit: false' so that increases latency as the runtime must fetch keys and warm the cache. sometimes transcription shows k v as 'k v cash' or other - just ignore.
[02:44] Tom: can you show where the per-token latencies are?
[02:48] Leo: sure - open the 'token timeline' panel - each token generation has its micro-timestamp, you can see a gap around tokens 14-18, which corresponds to a spike in kernel scheduling on the node. that's why response truncated.
[03:10] Maya: i'll pause - a lot of customers I talk to assume partials are model hallucinations; often it's infra. this view helps you narrow it quickly.
[03:22] Ana: what about when it's a routing fallback? like you said you have fallback policies to cheaper models, how's that recorded?
[03:29] Leo: good question. in the request detail we log the routed_model_id and the fallback_reason. you'll see fields: routed_model: 'gptx-compat-8q', fallback_to: 'gptx-quant', fallback_reason: 'capacity_shortage' and the console highlights a drop in token throughput.
[03:49] Tom: hmm we do run mixed models for cost so useful. can the console replay the request with the original KV state?
[03:55] Leo: yes, we have a sandbox replay that can rehydrate prefix cache from a saved snapshot if you consent to that data - it's opt-in. any cached K/V items are redacted in UI if they contain sensitive keys; we also support on-prem-only replays for air-gapped.
[04:12] Priya: that redaction part is important. do you integrate with our KMS?
[04:17] Maya: yes, we have KMS integrations and can map to customer-managed keys; we'll send the security doc that lists supported providers.
[04:25] Ana: great.
[04:30] [06:00] Speaker 3: background noise
[06:12] Leo: moving on - i'll trigger a guided replay now. first we fetch the request trace and generate a hypothesis - in this instance the runtime timed out on an internal gRPC call. watch the timeline, you'll see the runtime retry loop at 00:24:12.
[06:30] Ana: is that retry count configurable? our infra policy wants fewer retries and faster failover.
[06:36] Leo: yes you can set retries per-route, per-customer tier. also we show historical metrics so you can tune safely.
[07:00] Maya: quick interruption - can we talk about observability exports? Tom, you mentioned Datadog; we can export spans to your APM or keep them in Redwood with retention policies.
[07:15] Tom: ideally both, we want a copy in our Datadog but with sensitive fields stripped.
[07:21] Leo: doable - you can configure field-level redaction and we pass on a sanitized span.
[07:30] Ana: any chance of false correlations between our service traces and model traces? we saw mismatched timestamps in an earlier POC.
[07:38] Leo: we add a correlation id at ingestion and also annotate with node-local clock offsets; but yes if customer clocks drift it can look odd - we surface clock skew warnings in the trace header.
[07:54] Priya: show the error analysis workflow end to end? like starting at an SRE alert and going to root cause?
[08:02] Leo: yes - step 1: alert -> open request explorer, step 2: group by client route, step 3: run trace correlation, step 4: hypothesis and replay. i'll demo an alert flow: alert from Sentinel says elevated 5xx for route /generate-email, click the link and you're in the console.
[08:27] [08:30] Maya: a note on naming - console links can be embedded in PagerDuty/Slack to expedite triage.
[08:35] Tom: nice. show when it's a model regression vs infra.
[08:40] Leo: in the 'comparison' tab we align the failing request against a golden run for the same prompt set; divergences are highlighted with a delta-score. if the delta is token-level and coincides with a change in model version, we tag it as a model regression. if token gaps line up with node CPU spikes we mark infra.
[09:05] Ana: what's the false positive rate on those heuristics?
[09:08] Leo: heuristic is tuned on historical runs — ballpark we see around 80% precision but you can add custom rules.
[09:15] [10:00] Speaker 1: uh hm
[10:12] Leo: demo: now i'm switching to the 'request logs' view - this shows raw request/response payloads (redacted) plus headers. here's an example where the client is passing a malformed system prompt which causes tokenization overhead. you can rerun with a normalized prompt in the replay.
[10:40] Tom: can we pipe that normalized prompt back to our staging to validate?
[10:44] Leo: yes, the replay can POST to a target URL in your staging cluster; we support safe-mode to prevent production writes.
[10:52] Ana: question on retention - how long are traces kept? we have compliance rules for 6 months.
[10:58] Maya: retention configurable per-account; we can do 6 months and longer in enterprise plan, and short-term for dev.
[11:06] Priya: and export to our long-term archive?
[11:08] Leo: S3 export with encryption is supported.
[11:15] Ana: good.
[11:18] [12:00] background hum
[12:05] Leo: show of hands - anyone wants to see KV cache internals now?
[12:09] Ana: yes please.
[12:12] Leo: here's the cache heatmap - per-key hit rate, size, eviction events. notice this customer bucket has high churn leading to cache misses for common prefixes. when miss rate exceeds threshold, we recommend warmers or prefix pinning.
[12:33] Tom: prefix pinning? explain.
[12:35] Leo: you can pin top-k prefixes for critical routes so they stay in cache on boot; there's a tradeoff with memory. console tells you estimated memory delta.
[12:46] Priya: can you alert when pinning would help?
[12:49] Leo: yes, we have an automated recommendation engine in Optimize that surfaces cache pin suggestions and expected cost savings.
[13:00] Maya: small aside - Optimize also gives quantization suggestions if customers want to trade a little quality for big cost wins, but we can talk later.
[13:12] Ana: back to replay - you mentioned redaction. how granular is it?
[13:16] Leo: field-level redaction by JSON path and regex. we keep an audit trail of who accessed redacted content.
[13:26] Tom: does audit include token-level exposures? we need to know if any customer PII was in generated output.
[13:31] Leo: yes, we flag generation outputs that match configured PII patterns and mark them in the audit log.
[13:40] [15:00] interruption - brief network hiccup, audio drop 22s
[15:25] Maya: ok jumping ahead - run through an incident recap. we annotate the timeline with RCA notes and you can assign tasks from the console.
[15:36] Ana: that's helpful for postmortem culture.
[15:40] Leo: show 'assign' now - i can add an item, tag Tom, and it shows up in the action list; also sends a link to the trace.
[16:00] Priya: can these actions sync with our Jira?
[16:04] Leo: yes Jira integration available.
[16:10] Tom: earlier you mentioned model variants and automatic fallback. what's the policy around quality regressions when falling back?
[16:18] Leo: fallbacks are configured with quality thresholds and can be auto-approved or require canary verification. if fallback triggers and a downstream eval set shows regression beyond tolerance, we can auto-roll back the fallback policy.
[16:35] Ana: cool. show us how to run a batch of failed requests through replay?
[16:40] Leo: use the 'bulk replay' feature - upload a CSV of request IDs, pick snapshot or live rehydrate, and a target model. we'll queue them and produce a coverage report.
[16:55] Tom: how long to run a 500-request batch?
[16:58] Leo: depends on model and tokens - for small prompts on Dedicated you'd see parallelism; we also show ETA.
[17:10] Maya: pause for objections - price and data control?
[17:14] Ana: price. and third-party exposure when using hosted.
[17:19] Maya: fair - Dedicated gives you committed capacity, predictable unit cost and private VPC. Private/corp can be on-prem if needed for strict regs. we'll share numbers.
[17:30] Tom: latency targets - if we get a dedicated pool, can you commit to 95th <200ms?
[17:34] Leo: we have per-contract SLOs and can set route-level SLOs; we usually benchmark with your real prompt set during pilot.
[17:45] Priya: what's the pilot look like?
[17:48] Maya: 2-week pilot, include a dedicated test pool, sample traffic replay, and shared dashboards. we'll run the Optimize recommendations and deliver a final report.
[17:58] Ana: ok sounds good.
[18:02] [20:00] crosstalk, laughter
[20:15] Leo: final quick thing - the trace exports are JSONL; if you need a relational view we also push to BigQuery.
[20:25] Tom: BigQuery is ideal for our analytics team.
[20:29] Maya: i'll note that.
[20:34] Ana: question - do you keep historical policy changes? we need audit for routing rules as they change.
[20:40] Leo: yes policy history is versioned and you can diff any two versions in the console.
[20:48] Priya: show the audit log UI?
[20:51] Leo: here's an example - who changed fallback policy, when, and the before/after.
[20:59] Tom: excellent.
[21:05] [25:00] long-ish example walkthrough continues, redacted here for brevity
[25:40] Maya: recap - next steps are sending pilot pricing, benchmark harness, and security doc. Leo will provide the sample scripts and Tom will collect failing request ids.
[25:54] Ana: timeline - can we have the pilot by Sept 20?
[25:58] Maya: yes that's our target.
[26:05] Priya: any blockers for compliance review?
[26:08] Maya: we'll include SOC2 scopes and a contact for the security team; if you need additional compliance clauses we'll loop legal.
[26:17] Tom: ok i'll collect the three requests and share with Leo.
[26:22] Leo: great, once we have those we can run targeted replays and produce the incident RCA.
[26:30] Maya: anything else?
[26:34] Ana: no, thanks, that was thorough.
[26:38] Tom: thanks all.
[26:45] Maya: i'll follow up with links and notes. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
